name: Thigh squeeze (quad set)
why: Switches on the thigh muscle that pain and swelling turn off, without bending the knee. A first step after a knee flare-up.
setup: Sit with your leg straight out in front, a small rolled towel under the knee.
cues: Push the back of your knee into the towel
Tighten the front of your thigh
mistakes: Lifting the heel instead of squeezing
feel: Tightening in the front of the thigh, with the kneecap drawing up.

media.credit: Video: NUH Physiotherapy - Static quadriceps (National University Hospital (NUH) Singapore)

name: Straight leg raise
why: Strengthens the thigh while keeping the knee straight, so there's very little load through a sore knee.
setup: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat, the other leg straight.
cues: Lift the straight leg to the other knee's height
mistakes: Letting the knee bend as you lift
feel: Work in the front of the thigh.

name: Band knee straightening
why: Trains the last bit of knee straightening, where the inner thigh muscle (VMO) works hardest, in a knee-friendly standing position.
setup: Loop a band around a sturdy post at knee height and behind one knee, facing the post.
Step back until the band pulls that knee slightly bent.
cues: Straighten the knee against the band
mistakes: Letting the band snap the knee forward
feel: Work in the front of the thigh just above the kneecap.
stopIf: Pain at the front of the knee above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: Standing Banded Terminal Knee Extension (Motus Rx Physical Therapy)

name: Wall sit (isometric hold)

defaultDose.effort: Knee discomfort up to 3/10 is OK

why: Holding a squat without moving loads the knee tendon and thigh muscles steadily. For patellar tendon pain, holds like this let you keep the tendon working when moving exercises hurt, and many people find the pain eases for a while afterwards.
setup: Stand with your back against a wall, feet about 30 cm in front of you and hip-width apart.
Slide down until your knees are bent to a depth that feels hard but not painful. Go no lower than thighs level with the floor.
cues: Knees in line with your toes
mistakes: Going so deep that the knee hurts
feel: Hard work in the front of the thighs. Mild knee discomfort that settles after the set is OK.
stopIf: Knee pain goes above about 3-4 out of 10, or is worse the next morning.
cautions: Skip it if the knee is hot or swollen.
references: Rio E, et al. 2015. Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med 49:1277-83. (Leg-extension isometrics; same principle.)

media.credit: Video: Isometric Wall Squat for Knee Pain, , San Antonio, TX Puckett Physical Therapy (Puckett Sports Rehab and Physical Therapy)

name: Spanish squat (isometric hold)

defaultDose.effort: Knee discomfort up to 3/10 is OK

why: The band holds your shins upright, so the thigh muscles and knee tendon do the work with less squeeze on the front of the knee. A favourite hold for patellar tendon pain.
setup: Loop a long resistance band (or strap) around a sturdy post and behind both knees.
Step back until the band is tight, feet hip-width apart.
Sit back as if into a chair, keeping your shins upright.
mistakes: Letting the knees drift forward past the toes
Anchoring to something that can move
feel: Hard work in the front of the thighs. Mild knee discomfort that settles after the set is OK.
stopIf: Knee pain goes above about 3-4 out of 10, or is worse the next morning.
cautions: Check the anchor is solid before leaning back.
references: Rio E, et al. 2015. Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med 49:1277-83. (Leg-extension isometrics; same principle.)

media.credit: Video: Spanish Squats - Isometric Exercise for Patellar Tendinopathy (The Knee Resource)

name: Slow squat to a chair
why: A slow, controlled squat to a chair builds thigh and tendon strength. Slow lifting with steadily heavier loads is a core treatment for knee tendon pain.
setup: Stand in front of a chair, feet shoulder-width apart, arms out in front for balance.
cues: Sit back slowly to touch the chair
feel: Work in the thighs and buttocks. Mild knee-tendon discomfort up to 3/10 is OK.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3-4 out of 10, or worse the next morning.
references: Kongsgaard M, et al. 2009. Corticosteroid injections, eccentric decline squat training and heavy slow resistance training in patellar tendinopathy. Scand J Med Sci Sports 19:790-802.

media.credit: Video: Chair Squat Exercise (Margaret Martin, Physical Therapist)

name: Slow goblet squat

defaultDose.load: Heavy enough that the last reps are hard

why: Heavy, slow squats are one of the best-tested treatments for patellar tendon pain: tendons get stronger with load, not rest. Add weight gradually over the weeks.
setup: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest, feet shoulder-width apart.
feel: Hard work in the thighs and buttocks. Mild knee-tendon discomfort up to 3/10 is OK.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3-4 out of 10, or worse the next morning.
references: Kongsgaard M, et al. 2009. Corticosteroid injections, eccentric decline squat training and heavy slow resistance training in patellar tendinopathy. Scand J Med Sci Sports 19:790-802.

media.credit: Video: Strength Training for Soccer Players: Goblet Squats (Fit for Life Physiotherapy)

name: Split squat
why: Builds single-leg strength in the thigh and glute, with balance help from the back foot.
setup: Stand in a long stride, back heel lifted, holding a wall if needed.
cues: Drop the back knee straight down
Push up through the front heel
feel: Work in the front-leg thigh and buttock.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: How To: Split Squat (Reload Physical Therapy and Fitness)

name: Reverse lunge
why: A lunge that's kinder to the knee than stepping forward, building strength for stairs, hills and running.
cues: Lower the back knee towards the floor
Push through the front heel to return
feel: Work in the front thigh and buttock.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: How To Perform The Reverse Lunge (Dr. Carl Baird)

name: Slow step-down
why: Lowering yourself slowly off a step trains control of the knee, hip and foot arch: the same job your legs do going downstairs and downhill.
setup: Stand on a low step on one leg, the other foot hanging off the front, holding a rail if needed.
cues: Lower the free heel slowly to the floor
Knee stays over your second toe
mistakes: Hip dropping on the free side
feel: Work in the thigh and buttock of the standing leg.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: Eccentric step down - Lower Body Exercise (Commons Clinic)

name: Step-up

defaultDose.load: Add a loaded backpack to progress

why: Trains exactly what climbing stairs and hills needs. Great preparation for hiking.
setup: Stand facing a sturdy step, box or stair.
cues: Step up through the whole foot
feel: Work in the thigh and buttock of the stepping leg.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.
